topic: HIV testing uptake in STI patients

audits.title: Improving uptake of HIV testing in patients with a confirmed STI.
audits.standard: National Sexual Health strategy HIV testing targets
audits.setting: GU clinic, St Thomas' Hospital, London

cycle1.result: HIV test uptake 18% overall, 14% in STI group, 33% in negative-screen group.

audits.intervention: Nurse-led asymptomatic screening, opt-out HIV testing, no routine pre-test counselling, results by post

cycle2.result: Uptake 53% overall (n = 573), 41% in STI group (n = 285), 65% in controls (P < 0.01).

audits.citation: Day S, Lakhani D, Hankins M, Rodgers CA. Improving uptake of HIV testing in patients with a confirmed STI. Int J STD AIDS. 2004;15(9):626-628. doi:10.1258/0956462041724325. PMID: 15339373.

audits.title: Audit of offering HIV testing in the genitourinary medicine clinic in Aberystwyth in 2003.
audits.standard: GU Medicine Good Clinical Care Standard 2: offering HIV testing
audits.setting: Genitourinary medicine clinic, Bronglais General Hospital, Aberystwyth

cycle1.result: 97.5% of new patients screened for STIs were offered HIV testing; uptake 70.3%.

audits.citation: Jones J, Peterson S, Watson P. Audit of offering HIV testing in the genitourinary medicine clinic in Aberystwyth in 2003. Int J STD AIDS. 2005;16(6):450-451. doi:10.1258/0956462054094033. PMID: 15969783.

audits.title: Audit on routine HIV testing in patients attending genitourinary medicine clinics.
audits.standard: Sexual Health Strategy 2001: all patients attending GU medicine clinics for a sexual health screen should be offered an HIV test

cycle1.result: Patients accepted HIV testing when offered routinely (figures not reported).

audits.intervention: Routine offer of HIV antibody testing to clinic attenders

audits.title: HIV testing in Scotland. Are we meeting the standard? BASHH Scotland national audit 2004.
audits.standard: Draft Scottish Sexual Health Strategy 2003: HIV test offered to all GUM attendees not known to be HIV positive presenting with a new STI; reasons for non-uptake recorded
audits.setting: Scottish genitourinary medicine clinics (BASHH Scotland national audit)

cycle1.result: Practice highly variable; overall Scottish GU clinics failed to meet the strategy standard.

audits.citation: Ross F, Wardle D, Currie A, Baguley S. HIV testing in Scotland. Are we meeting the standard? BASHH Scotland national audit 2004. Int J STD AIDS. 2006;17(9):627-628. doi:10.1258/095646206778113168. PMID: 16981318.

audits.title: Completion of a British Association for Sexual Health and HIV regional audit loop: HIV testing in genitourinary medicine clinics in Scotland in 2004 and 2008.
audits.standard: Recommended HIV test offer and uptake in new attendees diagnosed with an STI
audits.setting: Genitourinary medicine clinics across Scottish health boards (BASHH Scottish Branch)

cycle1.result: Baseline test offer and uptake rates (figures not given in abstract).

cycle2.result: Large increases in rates of test offer and uptake, especially in boards with low baseline testing; overall rates remain below recommended levels.

audits.title: Audit of the effect of electronic patient records on uptake of HIV testing in a level 3 genitourinary medicine service.
audits.setting: Level 3 genitourinary medicine service, Royal South Hants Hospital, Southampton

cycle1.result: HIV test uptake 72.8% with paper records.

audits.intervention: Introduction of an electronic patient record, then modification of the EPR.

cycle2.result: Uptake rose to 78.1% after EPR introduction in 2010 (p = 0.009) and to 86.6% after EPR modification in 2012 (p < 0.0001).

audits.other_findings: Three cycles: 2007 paper, 2010 EPR, 2012 modified EPR.
audits.citation: Clarke E, Bhatt S, Patel R, Samraj S. Audit of the effect of electronic patient records on uptake of HIV testing in a level 3 genitourinary medicine service. Int J STD AIDS. 2013;24(8):661-665. doi:10.1177/0956462413478877. PMID: 23970576.

audits.title: BASHH 2016 UK national audit and survey of HIV testing, risk assessment and follow-up: case note audit.
audits.setting: UK sexual health clinics (BASHH 2016 national case note audit)

cycle1.result: Discrepancies between practice and clinic policies on enquiry about alcohol, recreational drugs and chemsex; previous testing commonest reason for refusing HIV test, though 33% of MSM had last tested over three months ago.

audits.other_findings: 21/119 declining due to window-period exposure had earlier risk not covered by previous testing.
audits.citation: Bhaduri S, Curtis H, McClean H, Sullivan AK. BASHH 2016 UK national audit and survey of HIV testing, risk assessment and follow-up: case note audit. Int J STD AIDS. 2018;29(11):1146-1150. doi:10.1177/0956462418767688. PMID: 29743005.

audits.title: The British Association for Sexual Health and HIV 2016 UK national audit and survey of clinic policies in relation to risk assessment, HIV testing and follow-up.
audits.setting: 142 UK sexual health clinics (BASHH 2016 national audit of clinic policies)

cycle1.result: No policy or agreed practice for alcohol enquiry in 24%, recreational drugs 21%, chemsex 43%; no policy on HIV test refusal in 13% for MSM and 18% for heterosexuals; 70% had HIV point-of-care tests.

audits.citation: Bhaduri S, Curtis H, McClean H, Sullivan AK, National Audit Group of the British Association for Sexual Health and HIV. The British Association for Sexual Health and HIV 2016 UK national audit and survey of clinic policies in relation to risk assessment, HIV testing and follow-up. Int J STD AIDS. 2018;29(11):1142-1145. doi:10.1177/0956462418771778. PMID: 29749877.
